text:
incident-bot: 🛎️ ALERT: Sev3 — GPU OOM during prefill on gpunode-17. Containers restarting (exit code 137). Affected service: runtime-prefill. Pager: @kevin_oncall.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: on-call handoff to @kevin_oncall (current shift).

kevin_oncall: I’m on pager. initial ask: which customers impacted and ETA on mitigation?

julie_ops: Seeing ~1200 5xx in the last 2m, spike started at ~12:03 UTC. 3 containers on gpunode-17 restarted in a loop, then spread to hotpool nodes 4/12.

alex_support: Customer check: AcmeAI and BetaSearch reported failures hitting /v1/generate with large prompts. Support ticket #12345 opened; Acme reporting ~30% of requests failing.

sam_infra: Quick log snippet from gpunode-17: 
```
[2026-03-17T12:04:12Z] runtime: ERROR: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 8.00 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total)
[2026-03-17T12:04:12Z] runtime: ERROR: Container exited with code 137 (OOM killer)
Stack: at runtime/prefill.cpp:prefill_kv_cache
```
No kernel driver resets, just OOM + SIGKILL.

maya_ml: Looks like large-context prefill is the trigger — customers are sending ~250k token prompts (PDF->prompt flows). KV cache spikes and nodes run out of memory while preallocating. This is prefill-time, not generation.

kevin_oncall: Ok. Mitigation options: 1) throttle/deny very large prefill requests at gateway, 2) route large-context to dedicated pool with >32GB GPUs or CPU fallback, 3) restart/replace nodes. Which can we do quickly?

nora_eng: I can push a gateway hotpatch to enforce PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=50k and reject >50k with 413. Rolling now to edge proxies. Patch: `gateway/config: max_prefill_tokens=50000` — pushing to canary then to prod.

julie_ops: Cordoning gpunode-17 to stop new pods there, scaling warm pool by +2 GPUs(large) to take spillover. Rolling restart of hotpool to pick up new gateway policy.

sam_infra: Applied cordon to gpunode-17. New pods are landing on hotpool-2/3 which have slightly more RAM.

incident-bot: Mitigation step applied: gateway-prefill-limit -> canary (12:12 UTC). Monitoring for error rate change.

kevin_oncall: Alex — please confirm AcmeAI receives a message about temporary limits and suggested retry window. Also add them to status page incident.

alex_support: Messaging now: "We’ve applied a temporary limit on extremely large prompts that can cause prefill OOMs. We’re working on targeted routing and will provide 30m updates." :email:

kevin_oncall: Any evidence of CUDA driver faults or memory leaks?

maya_ml: No driver faults in dmesg. This reads like natural KV-cache blowup during prefill for long documents. Longer-term: we need KV trimming, prefetch sampling, and a prefill memory safety limit inside the runtime.

nora_eng: Canary patch is green after 3 minutes — error rate on canary decreased ~92% for canaried traffic. Scheduling global push in 2 mins.

julie_ops: Global push done at 12:16 UTC. Error rate dropped ~80% across fleet. Some tail customers still hitting older edge nodes; flushing cache and restarting a few nodes clearing those.

kevin_oncall: Good. Current status: mitigation in place (gateway limit), cordoned node removed from rotation, scaled warm pool. Customer impact reduced but not fully resolved. Keeping Sev3; aiming to resolve in 30–60m.

sam_infra: Quick note: extracted OOM traces from nodes — attaching to ticket. Suggest we keep gpunode-17 offline for a health check.

incident-bot: Update: error rate decreased from 1200 5xx/min to ~220 5xx/min in 8m after hotpatch.

alex_support: AcmeAI acknowledged the mitigation and is testing. They see fewer failures but slower retries.

kevin_oncall: Next actions for postmortem: - full trace of prefill memory accounting - hotspot customers list - add runtime guard to refuse prefill > configured bytes - consider autoscale policy adjustment for prefill spikes - customer communications follow-up. Assign owners: maya_ml runtime safety, nora_eng gateway hotpatch, sam_infra node health.

nora_eng: I’ll open PR to add a hard prefill allocation cap + feature flag. Planning a runtime-side guard for 24–48h cadence.

maya_ml: I’ll prototype KV trimming heuristics and smaller-PM models for long-doc paths.

julie_ops: I'll coordinate on-call rotation notes and update the incident timeline for the handoff.

kevin_oncall: Thanks team. I’m going to keep watch for the next 30m and will escalate to Sev2 if we see a reversion. :white_check_mark:

alex_support: FYI support updated status page and notified 3 affected customers.

kevin_oncall: Closing loop — prepare a short blameless postmortem and include recommended runtime guard PRs. Marking incident as "mitigated" for now, will transition to follow-up tasks.
